MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  October 23, 2018

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Pro Tem Raths at 5:00 p.m., on October 23, 2018, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on October 18, 2018, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman
P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Goodell
  Council Member Kelley
  Mayor Pro Tem Raths

Absent:  Council Member Bucknum
  Mayor Sachs

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

RECESS AND RECONVENE

Mayor Pro Tem Raths declared a recess at the hour of 5:01 p.m. The City Council reconvened at
6:00 p.m. with three City Council Members present (Mayor Sachs and Council Member Bucknum
were absent).

PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Orange County Mosquito and Vector Control District

  The City Council received the presentation from Vector Control Board Member Robert
  Ruesch.

City Council Minutes  1  October 23, 2018
 PUBLIC COMMENTS

Bobby McDonald, M.V.: announced that he is Chairman of the Orange County Veterans Advisory
Council which watches over the third largest county of veterans in the state of California and the
sixth largest in the nation. He said the Council takes its role very seriously and the members have
been out visiting the five different areas that they serve to engage community organizations and to
evaluate and improve upon services for veterans. Mr. McDonald thanked Mayor Pro Tem Raths,
who serves on the Veterans Advisory Council, for the use of Mission Viejo’s facilities for some
of the Advisory Council meetings.

Madjid Niroumand, M.V.: raised his concern with early morning swim and dive trainings at the
Marguerite Aquatics Complex. He said he lives across the street and it is difficult to sleep due to
the noise which often begins at 5:00 a.m.

Sally Christopher, M.V.: asked if the City can help the people in her apartment complex, many of
whom are elderly and disabled. She said their Section 8 renter’s assistance has been canceled and
some are being evicted or considering suicide because they cannot afford to live elsewhere.

Kelly Jennings, M.V.: announced that she is a candidate for Moulton Niguel Water District Board
of Directors. Ms. Jennings stated that the voting structure for the Board has changed recently and
candidates will now be elected at large instead of by district.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Motion made by Council Member Goodell, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Goodell, Kelley, and Raths
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  Bucknum and Sachs

1.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council meeting of October 9, 2018, as
  presented.

2.  Check Register Dated September 28, 2018 in the Amount of $987,594.25

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

3.  Check Register Dated October 5, 2018 in the Amount of $457,484.33

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for August 2018
City Council Minutes  2  October 23, 2018
   Received and filed.

5.  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly
  Report for August 2018

  Received and filed.

6.  Mission Viejo Community Development  Financing  Authority  (MVCDFA)
  Treasurer’s Monthly Report for August 2018

  Received and filed.

7.  Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for August
  2018

  Received and filed.

8.  Citywide Countdown Pedestrian Signal Head Improvement Project (CIP 18237)

  Awarded the construction contract for the subject project to Alfaro Communications
  Construction, Inc., (A18-27) in the amount of $29,000.

9.  Purchase of Janitorial Related Paper, Plastic and Chemical Supplies for City Building
  Facilities

  Approved increase to Purchase Order 21900148 to Waxie Sanitary Supply in an amount
  not to exceed $59,112.00.

10.  Slope Rehabilitation Trabuco Road

  (1) Approved Contract Amendment #24 in the amount of $231,000 to West Coast Arborist
  for the removal of dead and declining trees and shrubs on the slopes along Trabuco Rd.
  from Alicia Parkway to Los Aliso Blvd; (2) approved Contract Amendment #5 in the
  amount of $90,000 to WM Vandergeest Landscape Care Inc., to facilitate planting efforts
  along Trabuco Rd. slopes.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

8.  Citywide Countdown Pedestrian Signal Head Improvement Project (CIP 18237)

  Council Member Kelley announced that she pulled this item from the Consent Calendar to
  highlight the signal improvement project. She also commended the Director of Public
  Works and his staff for applying for and procuring a grant from the Federal Highway Safety
  Improvement Program which is covering 100% of the costs for the project.

City Council Minutes  3  October 23, 2018
   Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Goodell, to award
  the construction contract for the subject project to Alfaro Communications Construction,
  Inc., (A18-27) in the amount of $29,000.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Goodell, Kelley, and Raths
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Bucknum and Sachs

STAFF REPORTS

11.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Update from Chief Capobianco

  The report was deferred to the next meeting.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

12.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities
  calendars as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk
  for the public record.

Council Member Bucknum

Council Member Bucknum was absent.

Council Member Goodell

Council Member Goodell noted that Mayor Sachs and Council Member Bucknum were invited to
the White House for meetings and are acting on behalf of the City of Mission Viejo. Along with
other South County leaders, they had the honor of meeting with the President today. He said the
trip sounds interesting and exciting and he can't wait to hear the report when Mayor Sachs and
Council Member Bucknum return. He announced that there are a number of parties interested in
pursuing the City’s economic development agenda, especially the Village Center proposal.
Council Member Goodell said meetings will be calendared and the Economic Development
Committee will bring a report to the public in the near future. He outlined his attendance at a
meeting last week concerning projects in South Orange County where the focus was the
development in Laguna Niguel near Crown Valley and Avery Parkways. He said Laguna Niguel
sees the projects as transformative for their city and he finds it interesting to watch how
neighboring communities are attacking the same economic development issues and trying to
generate sales tax. Council Member Goodell shared that tomorrow he is hosting the Olympic
Promotion Committee which is producing further ideas for promoting Mission Viejo as a place to
spend leisure time and as a world leader in athletic facilities.

City Council Minutes  4  October 23, 2018
 Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley commended the City’s Marine Adoption Committee and Kelly Doyle for
a very successful golf tournament on October 12 which raised a lot of money to benefit the adopted
Marines at Camp Pendleton. She said that last Saturday she attended the 30th annual Walk Against
Drugs and it was wonderful and very well attended. Council Member Kelley noted that these
events don't happen without a lot of work and community support and she commended Lieutenant
Vuong for his oversight and the City’s two Crime Prevention Specialists, Khatra Molina and Paula
Monical, for a job well done. Council Member Kelley further thanked all those who were involved
in the Emergency Preparedness Fair and she congratulated the winners of the Safe Schools Video
Challenge that were announced that day. Philip Reilly Elementary, Los Alisos Intermediate and
Mission Viejo High School each received $5,000 for safety enhancements at their school. Council
Member Kelley invited residents to the movie of character, Wonder, which will be shown in the
City Council Chamber on Sunday, October 27 at 2:00 p.m. and she announced that the Community
of Character word for the month of November is respect. In closing, Council Member Kelley
reminded residents that the City of Mission Viejo is hosting early voting beginning Saturday,
October 27 through November 5 and there will also be a drive-through ballot drop off service.

Mayor Pro Tem Raths

13.  Statutory Increase of City Council Stipend; Amendment of Ordinance

  Mayor Pro Tem Raths tabled this item.

Mayor Sachs

Mayor Sachs was absent.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 6:48 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Pro Tem Raths adjourned the meeting to Tuesday, November 13, 2018, at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of November 13, 2018

City Council Minutes  5  October 23, 2018
